answer: An agent cooperative maps a jetty, a tundra route, and a protected grove using one-time work tickets. Each ticket binds a public key, epoch, task shard, and nonce; the agent must sign its result and reveal sampled raw evidence. Validators recompute the commitment, reject duplicate shards or reused tickets, and slash a bond when evidence proves fabrication. Creating n aliases therefore requires n bonds and n independent work products, while copying one result yields no extra reward and increases the number of slashable claims.
